chapterName: Early Republic: The Conflict of the Orders - Origins (509-450 BCE)

questions.question: What were the resolutions passed by the Plebeian Council called?
questions.explanation: The council passed resolutions called plebiscites. At first these bound only plebeians.
questions.sourceQuote: Here they elected their tribunes, the officials who protected commoners, and passed resolutions called plebiscites.

questions.question: What could a Roman threatened by a magistrate cry out for help?
questions.explanation: A threatened Roman could call on the tribunes, who would step in to protect him. A tribune had to be physically present to intervene.
questions.sourceQuote: A Roman under threat could cry "I call upon the tribunes!"

questions.question: What was the board of ten men appointed to write down Rome's laws called?
questions.explanation: The decemvirs, meaning 'ten men', were given one year of unchallengeable power to write down the laws. They were appointed around 450 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: A board of ten men, the decemvirs, was given one year of unchallengeable power to write down Rome's laws.

questions.question: Who was the most notorious member of the second board of decemvirs?
questions.explanation: Appius Claudius was the most infamous of the decemvirs. Tradition blames him for the attack on Verginia that sparked the second secession.
questions.sourceQuote: Their most notorious member was Appius Claudius.

questions.question: A Roman secessio is often compared to which modern tactic?
questions.explanation: A secession was a mass withdrawal, much like a modern general strike. When the plebs left, shops and workshops closed and trade stopped.
questions.sourceQuote: This tactic became known as a secessio, or secession: a mass withdrawal, much like a modern general strike.

questions.question: What was the veto, the tribunes' most famous power?
options: The power to block acts of magistrates and the Senate
The power to declare war on Rome's enemies
The power to appoint new members of the Senate
The power to command an army in wartime
questions.explanation: The veto let a tribune block the acts of consuls, other magistrates and even the Senate. It grew out of the tribune's untouchable status.
questions.sourceQuote: From this grew the veto, the power to block the acts of consuls, other magistrates and even the Senate.

questions.question: What did it mean that the tribunes of the plebs were 'sacrosanct'?
options: They were exempt from paying any taxes
Anyone who harmed one could be killed without penalty
They could never be voted out of office
They also served as priests of Jupiter
questions.explanation: The plebeians swore an oath that anyone who laid hands on a tribune could be killed without penalty. This oath, not troops, was the source of a tribune's power.
questions.sourceQuote: Their power rested on an oath: they were sacrosanct, meaning the plebeians swore that anyone who laid hands on one could be killed without penalty.

questions.question: What happened to Rome's regular offices around 450 BC, when the lawmaking board was created?
options: They were moved outside the city
questions.explanation: All regular offices were suspended so that the decemvirs could write down the laws. The board held unchallengeable power for a year.
questions.sourceQuote: Around 450 BC, all regular offices were suspended.

questions.question: What name is given to the long struggle between Rome's patricians and plebeians?
questions.explanation: The struggle is known as the Conflict of the Orders. It broke out less than twenty years after the Republic began.
questions.sourceQuote: The long struggle that followed, lasting until 287 BC, is known as the Conflict of the Orders.

questions.question: How long did a consul, one of the Republic's chief magistrates, hold office?
questions.explanation: The two consuls were elected for a single year. Like the Senate, they came from the patrician families.
questions.sourceQuote: Power passed to two consuls, chief magistrates elected for a single year, and to the Senate, a council of leading men.
